Paylor Director October 13, 2011 Mr. Michael Stark Chief Facilities Engineer VISA, Inc. 45005 Russell Branch Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia 20147 Dear Mr. Stark: Registration No.: 73643 This letter acknowledges receipt of the supplemental information that you submitted on August 22, 2011 concerning your permit application dated June 30, 2011 to amend your permit to construct and operate a data center facility located at 45005 Russell Branch Parkway in Ashburn, Virginia. The Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) Northern Regional Office staff has reviewed your application in light of the new information. Based on that review, it does not appear that the facility calibrated the Flo-Scan meters in accordance with approved procedures (and/or manufacturer's written requirements or recommendations) as stated in the Warning Letter dated September 19, 2011, issued by DEQ to VISA, Inc. In light of this information, DEQ's Air Permitting division cannot proceed with the permit amendment to update the pound per gallon emission factors used to calculate annual emissions, as stated in your June 30, 2011 letter request. Should VISA, Inc wish to move forward with updating the emission factors contained in the current permit, the facility will need to have the fuel flow monitoring device recalibrated in accordance with manufacturer's approved procedures. The re- calibration shall be completed and certified by the manufacturer of the fuel flow monitoring device or an approved third party. Once recalibration has been completed, VISA may then restack-test the engines in accordance with Conditions 12 and 13 of the facility's August 28, 2009 (as amended April 29, 2010) NSR permit to obtain an acceptable pound per gallon emission factor for use in calculating annual emissions. Once completed, you may resubmit your amendment request for consideration.

corrections.new_text: 4. Emergency Generator Operation – The operation of the electric power generators (units 1 through 12) is limited to emergency situations. Emergency situations include emergency generator use to produce power for critical networks or equipment (including power supplied to portions of a facility) when electric power from the local utility (or the normal power source, if the facility runs on its own power production) is interrupted. The electric power generators (units 1 through 12) may be operated for the purpose of maintenance checks and readiness testing, provided that the tests are recommended by Federal, State, or local government, the manufacturer, the vendor, or the insurance company associated with the engine. Maintenance checks and readiness testing of such units is limited to 100 hours per year. The permittee may use the emergency generators (units 1 through 12) for additional hours to be used for maintenance checks and readiness testing, if the permittee maintains records indicating that Federal, State or local standards require maintenance and testing of the emergency generators (units 1 through 12) beyond 100 hours per year.
